title: Younger Kids Feel Excited About AI Stories, Study Says
summary:
How do kids feel when they watch videos or stories made with artificial intelligence, or AI? A new study says it depends on how old they are.

The study came from UCLA and the Center for Scholars and Storytellers. It asked young people ages 10 to 24.

More than half, 53.8 percent, said AI stories made them feel "fascinated" or "excited." About 32.1 percent felt "doomed" or "scared."

Younger kids felt better about AI. Only 9.7 percent of 10- to 13-year-olds picked "doom." Nearly half of them felt excited. Older teens and young adults picked "doom" more often.

Many of these feelings come from silly AI videos on social media, like clips of talking fruit.

One 13-year-old said AI should be shown in a fair way, with both good sides and risks.

The study also found that more than half of young people would most like to see a movie in a theater with friends.
why_it_matters: Thinking about how AI videos make you feel can help you use them wisely.
